description: Data Duplication Village at DEF CON 26 covers data storage security, forensics, and management with 4 talks on distributed file systems, cold storage forensics, cyberwarfare strategies, and large-scale storage management.

talks.title: Owning Gluster FS with GEVAUDAN
talks.summary:
### Attack Surfaces in Distributed Storage Clusters
At 00:00, security researcher Mauro Caseres demonstrates vulnerabilities in GlusterFS distributed file systems and introduces the GEVAUDAN exploitation toolkit at the Data Duplication Village. Caseres highlights how distributed storage clusters represent critical infrastructure targets.

### GlusterFS Architecture and Containerized Environments
At 05:08, the presentation examines GlusterFS clustering architecture. Caseres explains how GlusterFS aggregates storage bricks across multiple network nodes using Docker containers and remote procedure call (RPC) daemons to serve petabyte-scale file systems.

### Remote RPC Vulnerabilities and Authentication Bypasses
At 10:31, Caseres demonstrates how default GlusterFS deployments (specifically version 3.8.8) expose unauthenticated RPC listener ports. An attacker with network access can send crafted RPC packets to query cluster topologies, read volume parameters, and interact directly with internal daemons.

### Exploitation Mechanics with the GEVAUDAN Framework
At 15:54, Caseres details the design of GEVAUDAN, an exploit toolkit designed to compromise vulnerable GlusterFS instances. He demonstrates how GEVAUDAN executes arbitrary commands, alters access control lists, and extracts stored files directly from network storage volumes.

### Metasploit Integration and Cluster Hardening
Concluding between 20:59 and 26:26, Caseres showcases both standalone Python and Metasploit implementations of GEVAUDAN. He outlines defensive mitigations, advising administrators to configure strict firewall filtering around RPC ports, enable TLS communication between nodes, and upgrade to patched GlusterFS releases.

talks.title: Facts figures, fun from managing 100000 HDDs
talks.teaser: Facts figures, fun from managing 100000 HDDs
talks.summary:
### Cloud Storage Reliability Across 100,000 Hard Drives
At 00:00, Andy Klein (Principal Cloud Storage Analyst at Backblaze) delivers an empirical analysis of hard drive reliability based on data collected from operating over 100,000 hard disk drives (HDDs) in high-density cloud data centers.

### Fleet Telemetry and Annualized Failure Rates (AFR)
At 11:01, Klein presents longitudinal failure statistics across more than 132,000 drives from major manufacturers, including Seagate, HGST, Western Digital, and Toshiba. He explains how Backblaze calculates Annualized Failure Rates (AFR) to benchmark drive reliability across multi-petabyte storage pods.

### Drive Bathtub Curves and Generational Differences
At 22:01, the speaker analyzes failure curves. While infant mortality spikes occur in early operating months, drive survival stabilizes before mechanical wear sets in after year four. Klein highlights noticeable performance variations between drive generations, noting HGST's sustained longevity and Seagate's marked improvements in later 8TB and 12TB enterprise lines.

### Predictive S.M.A.R.T. Metrics for Imminent Drive Death
At 33:03, Klein details S.M.A.R.T. telemetry. Backblaze's statistical models reveal that among dozens of recorded attributes, five specific metrics strongly predict drive failure: S.M.A.R.T. 5 (Reallocated Sectors), S.M.A.R.T. 187 (Reported Uncorrectable Errors), S.M.A.R.T. 188 (Command Timeout), S.M.A.R.T. 197 (Current Pending Sectors), and S.M.A.R.T. 198 (Offline Uncorrectable Sectors).

### Supply Chain Economics and Helium-Filled Drives
Concluding between 44:01 and 55:00, Klein recounts operational history, including the 2011 Thailand floods that forced engineers to buy retail drives at consumer big-box stores ("drive farming"). He concludes by evaluating the thermal and energy advantages of modern sealed helium drives over traditional air-filled models.
